approachQuestion.prompt: A string over the three-character alphabet {(, ), x} is valid when it contains exactly one value. A value is x or an opening parenthesis, zero or more values, and a closing parenthesis. Return whether the entire string is valid. Examples: (x()) is valid; ()x, (x, and )( are invalid; the empty string is invalid.
constraints: String length is n with 0 ≤ n ≤ 100000; parenthesis nesting depth never exceeds h ≤ 1000, even for invalid input.
The alphabet is exactly the three characters (, ), x. Character access and index updates take constant time.
Do not modify or copy the input string.

options.text: Use that complete parser, but at every entry copy the remaining substring and parse within the copy.
options.feedback: This still checks the grammar and trailing input, but repeated suffix copying is avoidable.

options.text: Use the complete parser for one value and accept on success without checking the final cursor.
options.feedback: ()x begins with a valid value but has an extra trailing value.

options.text: Accept any string with equal counts of opening and closing parentheses, ignoring x positions and order.
options.feedback: )( has equal counts but cannot begin a valid value.

options.text: Parse one value with an index cursor: consume x, or consume (, parse children until ), then consume it. Fail on unexpected end or character. Accept only if parsing succeeded and the returned cursor equals the string length.
options.feedback: The local grammar and the final cursor check jointly reject both malformed nesting and extra values.

feedback.reason: Parsing one valid prefix does not prove the whole string is valid.
details: Parse with one shared string and a cursor. An x consumes one character. An opening parenthesis consumes values until its matching closing parenthesis; missing closers and unexpected characters fail. Parsing failure propagates immediately. The outer caller accepts only a successful single value ending exactly at n.

Parsing one valid prefix does not prove the whole string is valid. Require the final cursor to equal n. A closer belongs to the current opened container, so unexpected or missing closers must propagate failure.

“Accept any string with equal counts of opening and closing parentheses, ignoring x positions and order.”: )( has equal counts but cannot begin a valid value.

“Parse one value with an index cursor: consume x, or consume (, parse children until ), then consume it. Fail on unexpected end or character. Accept only if parsing succeeded and the returned cursor equals the string length.”: The local grammar and the final cursor check jointly reject both malformed nesting and extra values.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n be string length and h its maximum parenthesis nesting depth. Index access and local work take constant time. Count recursive frames; exclude input and returned boolean. No slices, hashing, or tail-call elimination. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: One cursor passes each demanded character once with nesting-depth frames.
details: A valid long string requires reading all characters; invalid input may stop earlier. Pending containers require one frame per nesting level.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested calls remain active along a path; their storage must be counted.
“O(n²) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: Each object is processed once without rescanning or copying its descendants.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: A shallow but wide input can still require inspecting every object.
